title: Exact geometric inverse image with arbitrary constant left-module coefficients
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, meaning an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on sheaves of sets with $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a unital ring $\Lambda$, not assumed commutative, in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. On each site let $\Lambda_{\mathcal C},\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$ be the sheafifications of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and use left-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $f^{-1}\Lambda_{\mathcal C}\cong\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$ carrying constant scalar sections to the same scalars. Applying $f^{-1}$ to addition, zero, negation and each scalar endomorphism defines a functor $f^*_{\Lambda}:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D})$. This functor is exact and, writing $V$ for forgetting scalars, has a canonical natural isomorphism $Vf^*_{\Lambda}\cong f^{-1}_{\operatorname{Ab}}V$. It identifies the forgotten module adjunction unit with the abelian inverse-image unit. These identifications commute with composition of geometric morphisms and with restrictions to localized sites. Thus termwise $f^*_{\Lambda}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms of complexes and induces inverse image on bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, parts (2), (5), (6), and its fixed-ring scalar-endomorphism proof; constant objects via the composite inverse image from the point

proof.text: Write $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$. By the constant-sheaf definition and sheafification universal property, maps from the constant set sheaf $\underline E$ to a sheaf $H$ are families, indexed by $e\in E$, of compatible sections of $H$, equivalently maps $*\to H$. Thus $\underline E$, with its scalar-section inclusions, is the coproduct of $E$ copies of the terminal sheaf $*$. The new ring-sheafification comparison identifies $|\Lambda_{\mathcal C}|$ and $|\Lambda_{\mathcal D}|$ with these constant set sheaves, including their scalar-section inclusions. The index set $\Lambda$ is small in the chosen coefficient universe. Since $L$ is a left adjoint it preserves this coproduct, and since it preserves finite limits it sends $*$ to $*$. The coproduct universal properties therefore give mutually inverse maps $c:L|\Lambda_{\mathcal C}|\to|\Lambda_{\mathcal D}|$ and $d$ carrying every scalar inclusion to the same scalar inclusion: each composite is the identity because it is so on every summand. No presheaf inverse image is used.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; Tag 00YR (gamma); coproduct preservation is Categories Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact

proof.text: Transport the ring operations by $L$ using its canonical terminal and product comparisons. For example the multiplication is $L(\mu)\circ p^{-1}$, where $p:L(A\times A)\cong LA\times LA$ and $A=|\Lambda_{\mathcal C}|$; zero and one use $L*\cong *$. Applying the functor to each ring-axiom diagram gives the same identities after these comparisons, so this is an associative unital ring sheaf, with no commutativity requirement. Check that $c$ respects operations. For constant scalar maps $s_a,s_b:*\to A$, functoriality and the product comparison give $L(\mu)p^{-1}(Ls_a,Ls_b)=L(s_{ab})$; after $c$ this is $s_{ab}$ on $\mathcal D$. The identical equation for addition has $a+b$ in place of $ab$, and constants and negation give $0,1,-a$. By the new comparison and the local-section theorem, sections of either constant ring are locally represented by constants. Two sections admit a common covering refinement; on it the preceding equations prove compatibility with each binary operation, and the sheaf uniqueness axiom then proves it globally. Thus $c$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism carrying each scalar to itself.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, ring sextuple paragraph; Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification

proof.text: The right adjoint $R$ preserves finite products. Apply the abelian-group-object adjunction lemma, and the equivalence between abelian sheaves and abelian group objects, to obtain $L_{\rm Ab}\dashv R_{\rm Ab}$ with the original underlying set functors, unit and counit. For a module sheaf $M$, its action is a sheaf map $a_M:\Lambda_{\mathcal C}\times M\to M$: this is sectionwise the action in the module definition, and semilinearity is precisely its naturality. On $LM$ define the action by $L(a_M)p^{-1}(c^{-1}\times1)$. Each module-axiom diagram uses only finite products, the ring operations and the action; applying $L$ and the comparisons proves its commutativity. Consequently this action, with the transported abelian operations, is a left $\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$-module sheaf. Applying $L$ to the action-compatibility equation for a module map proves that its image is linear, so this defines $f^*_{\Lambda}$. Forgetting its action leaves exactly $L_{\rm Ab}M$. Evaluating the action on a constant scalar $a$ shows that its unary scalar map is $L(\lambda_a)$, as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proof of (2), ring paragraph, and fixed-ring module paragraph

proof.text: Define the module direct image as follows. The canonical ring map $\gamma:\Lambda_{\mathcal C}\to R\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$ is $R(c)\circ\eta_{\Lambda_{\mathcal C}}$. Naturality of $\eta$ with respect to each ring operation, together with its product comparison, shows it is a ring map; composing with $R(c)$ preserves this property. Explicitly for a binary operation $m$ the identity is $\eta_A m=R(L(m)p^{-1})\,\rho^{-1}(\eta_A\times\eta_A)$, where $\rho:R(LA\times LA)\cong RLA\times RLA$; zero and one use the terminal comparison. These identities follow by naturality of $\eta$ for $m$ and for the two projections. For a module $N$ on $\mathcal D$, give $RN$ the action $R(a_N)\rho^{-1}(\gamma\times1)$. The product-preserving functor $R$ sends the module-axiom diagrams to commuting diagrams, and restriction along the ring map $\gamma$ gives the asserted module axioms. The same formula on maps defines a functor $f_{*,\Lambda}$ with underlying $R_{\rm Ab}$. On constant scalars its unary action is $R(\lambda_a)$, since $\gamma$ carries a constant scalar to its direct-image scalar section.

source.place: Tag 00YV, induced adjunction and its fixed-ring module paragraph; unit naturality with finite products

proof.text: For an abelian map $\alpha:L_{\rm Ab}M\to N$, put $\beta=R_{\rm Ab}(\alpha)\eta_M$. Naturality of the abelian adjunction bijection gives $\operatorname{adj}(\alpha\circ L\lambda_a)=\beta\circ\lambda_a$ and $\operatorname{adj}(\lambda_a\circ\alpha)=R\lambda_a\circ\beta$. Its injectivity therefore says that $\alpha$ commutes with every constant scalar if and only if $\beta$ does. A natural abelian map between constant-ring module sheaves commuting with the constant scalars commutes with every scalar section: represent that section by constants on a cover using the new sheafification comparison and the local-section theorem, use naturality and constant-scalar linearity there, and glue the equality. This applies on both sites, so the abelian hom bijection restricts to module maps, with the same inverse. It gives $f^*_{\Lambda}\dashv f_{*,\Lambda}$; its unit is the image of the identity under this restricted bijection, hence has underlying map $\eta_M$. Thus $Vf^*_{\Lambda}\cong L_{\rm Ab}V$ is natural and carries the module unit to the abelian unit.

source.place: Tag 00YV, adjunction assertion (2), (6) and fixed-ring proof; Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification

proof.text: We prove exactness for the given geometric morphism, without assuming a presenting continuous functor between these particular sites. Kernels of abelian-sheaf maps are sectionwise kernels and their underlying sets are equalizers of the given map and zero. The finite-limit-preserving $L$ sends this equalizer and its transported group operations to the kernel of the transported map. Hence $L_{\rm Ab}$ preserves kernels. It preserves cokernels because it is a left adjoint, by the preceding abelian adjunction and preservation of colimits. It is additive: addition of maps is addition on the target composed with their pair, and both addition and the product pairing are transported by $L$. Thus $L_{\rm Ab}$ is exact. The forgetful module functor is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels, and its statement identifies them with those in abelian sheaves. Since $Vf^*_{\Lambda}=L_{\rm Ab}V$, a sequence and its module inverse image have the corresponding abelian exact sequences. Faithfulness detects the vanishing of the kernel/image quotient. Therefore $f^*_{\Lambda}$ is additive and exact.

proof.text: For composable geometric morphisms, take the canonical direct-image comparison and the composite adjunction. The composite unit is $\eta^{gf}_M=g_*(\eta^f_{g^{-1}M})\circ\eta^g_M$, with the appropriate direct-image identification. The conjugate-isomorphism lemma characterizes the inverse-image comparison as the unique map satisfying its unit equation. Applying this lemma first to abelian and then to module adjunctions gives the same underlying comparison, since step 5 identifies their hom bijections and units. In particular it commutes with scalar maps and gives the natural module comparison. The coefficient-ring comparisons also agree: the two possible maps on the constant ring agree on every terminal-sheaf scalar summand of step 1, hence agree. For three morphisms both parenthesized comparisons satisfy the same composite-unit equation, so uniqueness identifies them; the identity comparison follows from the identity adjunction. This proves the claimed composition coherence, including that for the forgotten units.

proof.text: For an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, let $u:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ forget the structure map. It is continuous: a covering over $V/U$ is exactly an underlying covering of $V$, and base change of that covering along $W/U\to V/U$ has underlying objects $W\times_VV_i$ and structure maps to $U$. It is cocontinuous: any covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ of the underlying object of $V/U$ lifts to the covering $\{(V_i\to V\to U)\to(V\to U)\}$ with exactly the same image family. These verify the two hypotheses of the continuous-cocontinuous topos-adjunction theorem. Applying that theorem gives an adjunction $j_U^{-1}\dashv j_{U*}$ with $j_U^{-1}H(V/U)=H(V)$ and $j_U^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Thus restriction on sets is indeed the inverse image of a geometric morphism, so the preceding construction applies to it. The slice remains small because its objects and morphisms are specified by objects and morphisms of the small site.

proof.text: For the localization geometric morphism established in step 8, its inverse image is sectionwise restriction. The localized-ringed-site definition gives the corresponding sectionwise ring and module operations. The restriction of the constant ring presheaf is the constant ring presheaf on $\mathcal C/U$, and the ring-sheafification-localization comparison identifies its sheafification with $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}|_U$, preserving the unit and thus each constant scalar. Consequently applying the construction to $j_U$ gives exactly restriction: its transported action is $a_{M,V}$ at $V/U$, and its underlying map on a morphism is that morphism at $V$. Apply step 7 to composites involving these localization inverse images. The coefficient identifications agree on constant sections, and the module comparisons are the uniquely unit-compatible comparisons. Hence the construction and its forgotten-unit comparison commute with restriction whenever the inverse-image composite is restricted to localized sites. This asserts compatibility of the canonical localization/composition comparisons; it does not identify unrelated site objects on the two sites.

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor-derived-factorization theorem to the exact additive functor of step 6 between the abelian module-sheaf categories. It sends quasi-isomorphisms of complexes to quasi-isomorphisms, so termwise application induces the derived inverse image, with its canonical termwise comparison and triangulated structure. The bounded-below theorem gives $H^r(f^*_{\Lambda}K)\cong f^*_{\Lambda}H^r(K)$ and hence preservation of every lower cohomological bound. Restricting therefore gives the functor on $D^+$. All comparisons already constructed are natural chain maps when applied degreewise, so they survive localization at quasi-isomorphisms with their same equations.
